Level: Intermediate (B1–B2)
Duration: 60 minutes
Topic: Professional introductions & professional background
Main objective: By the end of the lesson, the student will be able to introduce themselves professionally, describe their current role and responsibilities, and talk about their professional experience.
1. Lead-in — Getting to Know Your Professional Profile
How long have you worked in your current position?
What did you do before your current job?

By asking these questions, the teacher activates the student's existing vocabulary and introduces the topic.
Business English: Introduce Yourself and Your Job
Students watch the following YouTube video and practice introducing themselves following the structure offered by the man from the video.
3. Reading — Meeting a New Business Contact

The student reads a short professional introduction in which a business professional introduces themselves, explains their current position, describes their responsibilities, and mentions their previous experience.

It is Monday morning, and Emma is attending a business networking event in London. She works as an Account Manager for BrightTech, a company that provides software solutions for small and medium-sized businesses.

Emma has worked in the technology industry for more than six years. She currently manages several international accounts and is responsible for maintaining relationships with existing clients. She also works closely with the sales and technical teams to make sure that clients receive the right solutions for their businesses.

Before joining BrightTech, Emma worked for a marketing agency, where she managed digital campaigns for international companies. She gained valuable experience in customer relations and project management during that time.
At the networking event, Emma meets Daniel, who works for a company that is looking for a new software provider.

Emma: Hi, I'm Emma. It's nice to meet you.
Daniel: Nice to meet you too. I'm Daniel. I work for Global Solutions.
Emma: Great. What do you do at Global Solutions?
Daniel: I'm a Business Development Manager. I mainly focus on finding new business opportunities and developing relationships with potential clients. What about you?
Emma: I'm an Account Manager at BrightTech. I manage several international accounts and work closely with our clients to understand their needs.
Daniel: Interesting. How long have you worked there?
Emma: I've been with BrightTech for almost three years. Before that, I worked in marketing for about four years.
Daniel: That's interesting. Have you worked with international clients before?
Emma: Yes, I have. I've worked with companies in Europe, North America and Latin America.
Daniel: That's great. We're actually looking for a software provider for one of our new projects. Maybe we could talk about it sometime.
Emma: Absolutely. I'd be happy to learn more about the project and see how we can help.

It's Monday morning, and the sales team at TechPro is having its weekly meeting. The Sales Manager, Sarah, is leading the meeting. Three Account Managers and a Business Development Executive are also attending.
Sarah: Good morning, everyone. Thanks for joining. Let's get started. The main objective of today's meeting is to review our sales performance and discuss our priorities for this week.
Sarah: First, let's look at last week's results. Tom, could you give us an update on your accounts?
Tom: Sure. I contacted five potential clients last week. Two of them are interested in our software solution. I'm planning to schedule another call with them this week.
Sarah: Great. What about the other three?
Tom: Two aren't ready to buy yet, and one client asked for more information about our pricing.
Sarah: Okay. Let's come back to pricing later. Maria, could you tell us about your biggest sales opportunity?
Maria: Yes. I'm working with a company that needs a new CRM system. They like our proposal, but they're concerned about the budget.
Sarah: I see. Do you think we can offer them a different package?
Maria: I think we could. From my perspective, a smaller package could be a good solution.
Sarah: I agree. Let's discuss that after the meeting. Now, let's move on to this week's priorities.
Tom: Can I raise a point?
Tom: I think we need to follow up with some of our older leads. We haven't contacted them recently.
Sarah: Good point. Let's make that an action item. Tom, could you prepare a list of the leads we need to contact?
Sarah: Great. So, to summarize, our priorities are following up with old leads, contacting new prospects, and preparing the new proposal. Let's meet again on Friday to review our progress.

Emma is a Sales Executive at TechSolutions, a company that provides software for small and medium-sized businesses. She is having a discovery call with David, the Operations Manager of a logistics company.
Emma: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. Before I tell you about our solutions, I'd like to understand your business and your current situation.
David: Sure. We're looking for a better way to manage our customer information.
Emma: I see. Could you tell me a little more about the problem?
David: At the moment, our information is in different spreadsheets. It's difficult for our sales and customer service teams to find the information they need.
Emma: So, one of your main challenges is having all your customer information in one place?
Emma: What are your main priorities at the moment?
David: We want to save time and improve communication between our teams.
Emma: And what would you like to improve specifically?
David: We'd like to respond to customers more quickly. At the moment, it can take two or three days to answer some requests.
Emma: I understand. What are your requirements for a new system?
David: It needs to be easy to use. We also need our sales and customer service teams to be able to access the same information.
Emma: That's helpful. Do you have any concerns about changing to a new system?
David: Yes. We're concerned about the cost and the time needed to train our employees.

Emma: That's understandable. So, if I understand correctly, your main priorities are improving communication, responding to customers more quickly, and saving time. At the same time, the solution needs to be easy to use and fit your budget.
David: Yes, that's exactly what we're looking for.
Emma: Great. Based on what you've told me, I think we may have a solution that could meet your needs. I'd like to show you how it works in our next meeting.

Emma is a Sales Executive at TechSolutions. She is having a discovery call with Michael, the Operations Director of a growing logistics company.
Emma: Hi Michael, thanks for taking the time to speak with me today.
Michael: You're welcome. We're interested in learning more about your software.
Emma: Great. Before I tell you about the product, I'd like to understand your current situation. Could you tell me a little about how you're managing your operations at the moment?
Michael: We're currently using two different systems. They're not well connected, and our employees have to enter the same information more than once.
Emma: I see. What would you say is your biggest pain point?
Michael: Definitely the amount of time we spend entering and checking information.
Emma: And what impact does that have on your business?
Michael: It slows our teams down and sometimes creates errors.
Emma: That makes sense. What are your main goals for a new solution?
Michael: We'd like to save time, reduce errors, and improve communication between our teams.
Emma: What are your main requirements?
Michael: The system needs to be easy to use and integrate with our existing software.
Emma: That's helpful. Do you already have a budget for this project?
Michael: Yes, but we need to stay within a specific budget.
Emma: Understood. And what is your timeline?
Michael: Ideally, we'd like to have a new system in place within three months.
Emma: Okay. And could you tell me a little about your decision process? Who else is involved?
Michael: Our IT Manager and Finance Director will also be involved. I'm responsible for evaluating the different options, but the final decision will be made by our CEO.

Emma: That's very helpful. So, if I understand correctly, your main goals are to save time, reduce errors, and improve communication. You need a solution that is easy to use, works with your existing software, and fits your budget and timeline.
Emma: Great. Based on what you've told me, I think our solution could be a good fit. Would it make sense to schedule a product demonstration next week?

Emma is a Sales Executive at TechSolutions. Last week, she had a discovery call with Michael, the Operations Director of a logistics company.

Michael explained that his company was using two different systems. The systems were not well connected, so employees had to enter the same information more than once. The company wanted to save time, reduce errors, and improve communication.
Today, Emma is presenting a solution to Michael and his team.
Emma: Thanks for joining today's presentation. Based on our previous conversation, I'd like to show you a solution that could help you improve your operations.
Michael: Great. We're interested in seeing how it works.
Emma: Let's start with one of your main challenges: entering the same information more than once. Our platform allows your teams to share information automatically between different departments.
Emma: One of the key features is our integration system. It connects with the software you're already using, so you don't need to replace everything.
Michael: That's important for us because we don't want to change our entire system.
Emma: Exactly. The main benefit is that your employees can access the same information without entering it again. This can save time and reduce errors.
Michael: What about communication between teams?
Emma: The platform also includes a shared dashboard. Everyone can see updated information in one place. This means your sales, operations, and customer service teams can work with the same data.
Michael: That could definitely improve communication.
Emma: Another benefit is the reporting function. The system automatically creates reports, so managers don't need to collect information manually.
Michael: How easy is it to use?
Emma: The platform has a simple, user-friendly interface. We also provide training and customer support during implementation.
Emma: Based on your needs, I'd recommend starting with our Professional Package. It includes the integration system, shared dashboard, automatic reporting, training, and customer support.
Michael: It sounds like a good fit for us.
Emma: Great. I'd be happy to arrange a demonstration so your team can see the platform in action.

Emma is a sales executive at TechSolutions. She has just presented a software solution to David, the operations director of a logistics company.
During the discovery call, David explained that his company wanted to save time, reduce errors, and improve communication between departments.
Emma has now presented the solution.
David: I like the solution, but I have a concern about the price.
Emma: I understand your concern. Could you tell me a little more about it?
David: Your professional package is more expensive than another solution we've been looking at.
Emma: I see. Is the main concern the total cost, or are you comparing the features with the other solution?
David: Mainly the total cost. We have a limited budget.

David: How much time could we actually save?

David: Yes, that would be helpful. Then I can discuss it with our Finance Director.
